blocks.p: The game itself shows what you carry in an inventory window and what is around you in a loot window. Each window shows one container at a time; to see another, click its button on the right edge of the window.

Figure 19-1 shows the two windows of the game itself, the inventory window at the left and the loot window at the right, each with its column of container buttons at its right edge. Only one container can be seen in each window.

caption: Figure 19-1
The game's own windows: inventory, left, and loot, right.

blocks.p: ZNIX shows the same things in two windows of its own, the *Character* window and the *World* window, and gives every open container a column of its own. Figure 19-2 on the facing page shows the same moment in ZNIX.

marks.text: Vanilla: an inventory window and a loot window. The buttons on the right edge pick a container.

sticky.text: The game's own: one container per window.

blocks.p: In ZNIX each open container sits beside the others as a column. The *Character* window holds what you carry: in Figure 19-2, the military backpack and the inventory. The *World* window holds every container in reach: the trunk of the car, a duffel bag and the ground.
Each column has a header with the name of the container, its weight against what it can hold, and the number of items in it. Below the header the items are listed, under column heads that sort them.

caption: Figure 19-2
The same moment in ZNIX: the Character window, left, and the World window, right.

blocks.p: To move an item, drag it to another column. The item goes into the container of the column you drop it on.

marks.text: Character window: the military backpack and the inventory, each in its own column.
World window: each container in reach has its own column: the trunk, a duffel bag and the ground.

sticky.text: In ZeD every container is a column.
